# Roadmap — pdf-integrity

Live milestones in `after` order, then standing tracks. Acceptance verdicts are computed
from evidence under the descendant-commit rule (D-016).

## Milestones

### M1 — factual audit utility

`proposed` · `@audit.milestone.m1-factual-audit/1`

A `pdf-cli audit` run (later `lege-pdf-audit inspect`) over any PDF emits a
versioned JSON and terminal report of neutral facts: SHA-256 and size, PDF
version and header offset, clean-versus-recovered parse with recovery events,
xref-section inventory, linearization, encryption, metadata and XMP inventory,
AcroForm, XFA, JavaScript, embedded-file and optional-content flags, annotation
objects with identity and forensic metadata, signature dictionary and ByteRange
inventory, per-page representation classification (Vector, RasterOnly,
RasterWithTextLayer, Mixed, Blank, Unknown), and font and image inventories.
This alone identifies PDF-Verse-style flattened output and most
explicit-annotation cases.

**Plan of record:** [M1 plan of record](ACTIVE-WORK.md#m1-plan-of-record) `@audit.work.m1-plan/1`

### M2 — correct logical revision history

`proposed` · `@audit.milestone.m2-revision-history/1` · after `@audit.milestone.m1-factual-audit/1`

The structure layer preserves per-section xref entries and the checker
reconstructs logical revisions correctly: classic and stream sections with
entries, hybrid /XRefStm grouping into one logical save, valid
startxref-plus-EOF boundary pairing, oldest-to-newest ordering, linearization
stubs distinguished from human edits, per-revision object changes classified as
Added, Redefined, Freed or RepeatedIdentically with raw and semantic hashes,
object-role classification, reverse object-to-page mapping, and PrefixSource
opening of any reliable historical revision through the ordinary
DocumentSnapshot path. When the xref was rebuilt by scanning, the report states
that original revision membership cannot be established.

**Plan of record:** [M2 plan of record](ACTIVE-WORK.md#m2-plan-of-record) `@audit.work.m2-plan/1`

### M3 — revision comparison and overlay evidence

`proposed` · `@audit.milestone.m3-diff-and-overlay/1` · after `@audit.milestone.m2-revision-history/1`

The checker compares consecutive logical revisions at three levels — object
diff, semantic diff (words, glyphs, fonts, images, page relationships) and
deterministic visual diff with connected changed-region extraction — and
detects overlays: annotation-on versus annotation-off render diffs intersected
with glyph boxes, underlying-text and appearance-text extraction, and
painter-order occlusion candidates for content flattened into page streams
(opaque rectangle, form XObject or image painted over earlier text). An
optional PageTrace provenance sidecar maps operators back to source stream
objects and byte spans in audit mode only. Findings ship with evidence PNGs or
SVG overlays. This milestone delivers the genuinely useful product: reports
like `previous "2.84" / current "3.84"` with page rectangle, object history
and revision index.

**Plan of record:** [M3 plan of record](ACTIVE-WORK.md#m3-plan-of-record) `@audit.work.m3-plan/1`

### M4 — signature verification

`proposed` · `@audit.milestone.m4-signatures/1` · after `@audit.milestone.m3-diff-and-overlay/1`

Signature reporting reaches both layers of the layering decision: strict
ByteRange validation against original bytes, association of each signature
with its logical revision, exact post-signature object-change lists, DocMDP
and FieldMDP policy parsing and compliance, then CMS/CAdES digest
verification, certificate chain and trust reporting, and timestamp status via
the chosen external cryptographic implementation. The report always keeps the
five statuses separate: digest valid, certificate trusted, certificate
time-valid, later revision present, later change permitted.

**Plan of record:** [M4 plan of record](ACTIVE-WORK.md#m4-plan-of-record) `@audit.work.m4-plan/1`

### M5 — consistency heuristics, validated against a legitimate corpus

`proposed` · `@audit.milestone.m5-consistency-heuristics/1` · after `@audit.milestone.m4-signatures/1`

The weak-signal layer for documents whose history is gone (full rewrite,
Save As): embedded font-program hashes and per-line font-identity outliers;
text-run spacing, matrix and TJ-style outliers against surrounding lines; font
subsets with unusual glyph coverage; stream-filter and serialization-style
outliers; resource-name and object-number clustering; metadata timeline
inconsistencies (CreationDate, ModDate, XMP, producer disagreement); image
DPI, codec, quantization and colorspace outliers; and producer fingerprints.
Every heuristic emits at ContextualIndicator or WeakHeuristic strength only,
and none ships until its false-positive rate is measured against the
legitimate-producer corpus of the fixture track.

**Plan of record:** [M5 plan of record](ACTIVE-WORK.md#m5-plan-of-record) `@audit.work.m5-plan/1`

### Fixture and legitimate-producer corpus

`proposed` · `@audit.track.fixture-corpus/1`

Standing collection work no milestone contains: extend pdf-test-support to generate controlled tampering fixtures (annotation-in-later-revision, appearance-over-text, white-rectangle-plus-text, same-font content redefinition, /Contents object-to-array change, image patch, full-page raster, OCR-layer-behind-image, metadata-only update, signature-only update, permitted form fill, post-signature edit, every xref variant, linearized and malformed forms), and continuously capture legitimate outputs from Acrobat, browser print-to-PDF, Chrome drawing, macOS Preview, Office, LibreOffice, scanner and OCR software, optimizers, signers, PDF-Verse, pdf-lib and jsPDF. Label every fixture with the operation that produced it, never with a fraud judgement.
